text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- One Albanian citizen was shot dead and two Macedonian soldiers were wounded in a shootout at the Macedonian-Albanian border. Macedonian police captured a group of 80 Albanians who were illegally staying in Macedonia.

- Most political parties in Macedonia do not support the protest rally to be organised on Thursday in Skopje by the largest opposition party IMRO-DPMNY under the slogan "stop economic and social collapse of Macedonia". They support IMRO-DPMNY demands but recommed a solution should be found through dialogue and institutions of the system.

- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski already had two rounds of talks with leaders of the opposition IMRO-DPMNY and Liberal Democratic Party, Ljubco Georgievski and Petar Gosev, on new electoral laws and possibility of holding early elections.
- Financial scandal breaks out in the Skopje parliament following an investigation showing that 23 million German marks are missing from the municipal budget.

- An anti-government rally is scheduled by the opposition IMRO -DPMNY for Thursday in Skopje at 1800 hours local time. Depositors of several bankrupt pyramid financial institutions and over 50,000 Macedonians are expected to attend. The rally was moved from March 27 because IMRO-DPMNY leader Ljupco Georgievski decided to give Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski time to resolve several financial scandals in the country.
- The ruling SDAM says IMRO-DPMNY would be to blame for possible incidents and destabilisation of the country as a consequence of the rally.

- The League of Democracy demands of President Kiro Gligorov to gather all political parties in the country to prevent demonstrations on Thursday. If he doesn't do this he and the government shall be responsible for the destabilisation of the country, it said. The party supports demands of IMRO-DPMNY. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
